test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 20 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Two trains 240 m and 320 m long are travelling on parallel tracks in the same direction at speeds of 59 km/h and 50 km/h. How long will it take for the two trains to pass each other from the instant they meet?
solution:
**Given:**

Length of Train A = 240 m

Length of Train B = 320 m

Speed of Train A = 59 km/h

Speed of Train B = 50 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Relative Speed

**Calculation:**

Total Distance to be covered = Length of Train A + Length of Train B

Total Distance = 240 m + 320 m

Total Distance = 560 m

Relative Speed = Speed of Train A - Speed of Train B

Relative Speed = 59 km/h - 50 km/h

Relative Speed = 9 km/h

Convert Relative Speed to m/s:

1 km/h = (5)/(18) m/s

Relative Speed = 9 × (5)/(18) m/s

Relative Speed = (45)/(18) m/s

Relative Speed = 2.5 m/s

Time taken to pass each other = Total Distance / Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 560 m / 2.5 m/s

⇒ Time = 224 seconds

Convert seconds to minutes:

1 minute = 60 seconds

⇒ Time = 224 / 60 minutes

⇒ Time = 3 minutes 44 seconds

**The correct answer is option 3.**
